Syria is a country in the Levant, between Turkey, Iraq, Jordan, Israel and Lebanon, with its capital at Damascus. It became independent from the French Mandate in 1946. The map shows it from 1945.

Its first years were unstable, with three coups in 1949 alone. In 1958 it merged with Egypt as the United Arab Republic under Nasser, but left in 1961. In 1963 the Ba'ath Party took power. In the Six-Day War of 1967 Syria lost the Golan Heights to Israel.

Hafez al-Assad seized power in 1970 and ruled until his death in 2000, drawing support from his own Alawite minority. In 1982 his army crushed an uprising in the city of Hama, killing thousands. His son Bashar succeeded him. When protests began in 2011 during the Arab Spring, the regime met them with force, and the country slid into the Syrian civil war. Hundreds of thousands died and millions fled, many to Turkey and Europe. Rebels overthrew Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.
sum: Syria is a country in the Levant, between Turkey, Iraq, Jordan, Israel and Lebanon, with its capital at Damascus. It became independent from the French Mandate in 1946. The map shows it from 1945.
